decision: Reject this direct-product version for runtime admission. It preserves all tested exact witnesses and saves requested allocations in six phases, but eight quadratic phases are slower in every fixed pair and fourteen phases in at least four. Multiradical, pi-transport and mixed-field costs remain unresolved under the performance-before-memory ladder. The favorable rows and unchanged measured retention do not erase those timing costs.
qualification: Both variants pass twenty shared projection/storage/memo/alias tests, eight shared direct-product controls, six inherited cache tests, eleven P4 tests and 28 doctests. Each passes 902 all-feature and 815 default library tests. Formatting, strict default/all-feature/all-target Clippy and warning-denied scalar docs pass. Counts overlap; these are not unique or full-workflow totals.
adverse_costs: Quadratic multiradical-square first and cloned queries are slower in all five pairs: median paired ratios 1.035270 and 1.075481, with ranges 1.012632..1.062424 and 1.047692..1.241560. Their requested memory counters match.

Quadratic pi-transport first/warm/cloned queries are slower in all five pairs: median paired ratios 1.039035, 1.035174 and 1.054946. Mixed-field-decline first/warm queries are also slower in all five, at 1.062335 and 1.060469. Their requested memory counters match.

Quadratic opaque-decline construction is slower in all five pairs, median paired ratio 1.041496. Opaque warm and cloned queries are slower in four pairs, at median paired ratios 1.231191 and 1.521822; variation is substantial and every sample remains.

Conjugate-then-affine cloned queries save allocations but are slower in three pairs. Their median paired ratio is 1.008369 while the ratio of medians is 0.981806. Both summaries and all paired observations remain visible.
favorable_costs: Rational conjugate-product first/warm/cloned phases save 1,000 requested allocations and 64,000 allocated bytes per 1,000 inputs. Quadratic conjugate-then-affine first/warm/cloned save 857 calls and 54,848 bytes. Every paired memory delta repeats five times. Retained bytes match in all phases; four phases reduce peak requested bytes by 64.

Quadratic conjugate-then-affine warm is faster in every pair, median paired ratio 0.944369. First queries are faster in three pairs; cloned queries in two. Rational conjugate-product first/warm/cloned are faster in four pairs each.

Other all-five-faster phases include rational multiradical-square cloned, quadratic-reciprocal warm/cloned, pi-parameter-transport first/warm, quadratic multiradical-square construction and integer wide-affine first. Complete favorable ranges remain attached.

Rational radical-Laurent warm/cloned are also faster in all five pairs, but their total phase medians are only about 15,000 to 16,500 ns across 4,096 inputs. These timer-scale rows are preserved without claiming a practical effect.

code_generation_observation.scope: Existing baseline and candidate quadratic timing binaries only; no additional cost sample.
code_generation_observation.interpretation: Both binaries contain separate coefficient and polynomial multiplier symbols. The coefficient body grows by 1,688 bytes and its first stack-pointer subtraction by 16 bytes. This motivates testing a helper boundary; it does not establish lost inlining, total stack use or the cause of a timing change.

next_step.task: Keep all sources and samples frozen. Review extracting the qualified direct arithmetic into a private non-inlined helper while leaving the original opaque guard, eligibility conditions and general fallback in the entry method. Establish ownership and bounds for the helper call before preparing any new source.
next_step.comparison: Use a fresh three-source experiment if that review succeeds: unchanged parent, this direct version as a control, and the extracted-helper candidate. Shared correctness tests and new fixed costs distinguish the source change from variation across separate historical runs.

limits: The comparison uses a new closed sample set. It neither extends previous samples nor establishes native workload performance.
Ratios, directions and ranges are descriptive; they establish neither statistical significance nor an application speedup. Every adverse row is retained.
Requested Rust heap counters exclude native C heaps, allocator bookkeeping and stack frames. Private coefficient layouts do not establish total memory or eventual reclamation.

Native qualification/cost controls, full reports, production CLI size, original full-fixture limits and the complete workflow matrix remain open. Dependencies, Box payloads and existing owned coefficient layouts are unchanged. The original cache-read lock lifetime is unchanged. Eligibility comparisons, code generation and reused vector capacities remain cost risks; native behavior still requires evidence.
Only the two existing quadratic timing executables are inspected. These are static symbol/disassembly observations, not a new timing or allocation sample.
Both multipliers have standalone symbols in both binaries. This does not prove which other call sites inline them and does not establish a lost-inlining explanation.
The first stack-pointer subtraction excludes register pushes, callees and dynamic path behavior. It is not a total stack-memory or peak measurement.
A larger body or frame can motivate an isolated helper-boundary experiment but cannot causally explain the measured slowdowns.
All six probe binaries grow by 1,968 to 1,984 bytes. These are probe sizes, not production CLI sizes.
Timing variation affects favorable and adverse rows. No sample is removed, appended or selectively repeated, and no statistical significance or native speedup is claimed.
The version 1 test-import failure and all of its sources/logs remain preserved. Version 2 changed only that import before qualification; candidate arithmetic remained unchanged.

Main runtime and all 35 original native paths remain unchanged. The full plan is incomplete; all 39 properties, 14 targets and crate future work remain in scope, with individual ledger statuses unchanged.
